entities.summary: Justyna Budzińska-Tylicka was a Polish physician and women's rights advocate, active in the interwar era. After earning a medical degree and practicing in Paris for seven years, she returned to Poland and practiced medicine in Warsaw. Active in the women's movement and the push for expansion of women's rights, she later served on the Warsaw City Council and was involved in social endeavors to improve both health and women's political involvement. One such initiative was opening the first birth control clinic in Poland and another was the founding of the Association of Polish Female Physicians.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent women's rights advocate and physician in interwar Poland, Justyna Budzińska-Tylicka played a crucial role in expanding women's rights and improving healthcare access. Her initiatives, including the establishment of the first birth control clinic in Poland and the Association of Polish Female Physicians, had a lasting impact on the country's social landscape.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a pioneering female physician in Poland, Justyna Budzińska-Tylicka's advocacy for women's rights and healthcare led to the establishment of the first birth control clinic in Poland and the founding of the Association of Polish Female Physicians, improving health outcomes and empowering women in her country.
